title: Pilot study for the evaluation of different sampling techniques guided by single-operator cholangioscopy in patients with indeterminate biliary strictures
summary:
It is often difficult to determine whether a narrowing of the bile duct is caused by a benign (non-cancerous) or malignant (cancerous) condition. A modern diagnostic procedure called cholangioscopy allows doctors to directly examine the bile ducts using a very small camera. During this procedure, tissue samples can be taken from suspicious areas for further analysis. However, malignant changes are not always detected reliably because the tissue samples obtained are often very small and only a limited number of samples can be collected.
The aim of this study is to identify the most effective tissue sampling technique during cholangioscopy. Improving the quality of tissue samples may increase the accuracy of diagnosing indeterminate bile duct strictures.
A total of 60 patients with an unexplained narrowing of the bile duct will participate in this study. All participants have an independent clinical indication for cholangioscopy with tissue sampling. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three different sampling techniques. The study will compare conventional single biopsies, the collection of multiple biopsies followed by aspiration, and a technique in which repeated biopsies are taken from the same location to obtain tissue from deeper layers.
The study will evaluate which technique provides the highest diagnostic accuracy for detecting malignant disease. In addition, the optimal number of tissue samples, the time required for tissue collection, and the frequency of procedure-related complications will be assessed. The results are expected to improve the diagnosis of bile duct strictures and support more accurate treatment planning for patients.

Study Objective
The primary objective of this prospective randomized pilot study is to identify the optimal SOC-guided tissue acquisition technique using designated biopsy forceps for the diagnosis of indeterminate biliary strictures.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
indeterminate biliary stricture, indication für ERCP with cholangioscopy
Exclusion criteria:
Patients with visible pancreatic head mass lesions (susp.pancreatic cancer), altered pancreatobiliary or duodenal anatomy (postoperative and others), contraindication to ERCP, evidence for intrahepatic metastases, septic cholangitis
